result.rationale: The diff at deleteEvent changes `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the predicate compares against null/undefined and always fails, so `calendarId` resolves to undefined and falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` — a regression from the prior behavior of using the destination calendar's externalId. Same dead-pattern also exists in updateEvent. Mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent`, the new fallback computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is absent/undefined, the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), so it will not match any real calendar and returns `undefined`. Given `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` is defined immediately above, deletion will then fall back to primary rather than using the intended destination calendar (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a real behavior regression visible in the diff.
